children: Democratic Senator John Fetterman, who has increasingly broken with fellow Democrats on issues including Israel, the Iran war and immigration, made a surprise video appearance at President Donald Trump's Republican midterm convention in Dallas on Wednesday.

"Yes, I'm Senator John Fetterman, Pennsylvania. Yes, I'm a Democrat. Why am I here talking to you today? Because, well, I'm a common-sense Democrat," said Fetterman, wearing his signature hoodie and standing in front of a steel plant as he introduced his Republican Senate colleague, Dave McCormick, also of Pennsylvania.

"I'm always going to stand with America. I'm always going to reject the extremes and socialism and that anti-American way of life," he added, while pledging to work with Trump to defend "the steel way of life" in western Pennsylvania.

A first-term lawmaker with an unpredictable streak, the 57-year-old Fetterman made his video appearance at the two-day event known informally as the "Trumpapalooza," which Republicans hope will shore up their chances of maintaining control of the Senate and House of Representatives in November's midterms.
Republicans hold a 53-47-seat Senate majority and have become increasingly vulnerable to Democratic gains in several swing states, according to independent political analysts.
Fetterman has denied speculation he may leave the party.
"I'm not going to be a Republican, but I'm going to be a Democrat that's going to have a conversation with whoever is playing it straight," Fetterman said in a recent interview with Fox News.

Fetterman’s readiness to buck his party has drawn comparisons with former Senators Joe Manchin and Kyrsten Sinema, Democratic centrists who became independents before leaving the Senate and repeatedly caused headaches for their party leaders during the first half of Democratic President Joe Biden's term.
By contrast, Fetterman has not used his position to leverage concessions from party leaders or to shape legislation. Instead, Fetterman maintains that he votes for what he thinks is true.

Known for his towering frame and fondness for wearing hoodies and gym shorts on the Senate floor, Fetterman built a working-class image that helped propel him to victory in 2022. But that image has given way to open conflict with his party's left flank.
In a recent Fox News interview, he described the rise of activism in the Democratic Party as "an orgy of socialism."

He has faced more intense hostility from party members in recent days, after a Wall Street Journal report in which former staff members and lawmakers claimed he had more interest in cultivating relationships with conservative commentators than in doing the job of senator. The Journal reported Fetterman did not respond to the paper's several requests for comment.
